transformers.note: Google model served remotely through YunZhu Hub's Gemini-native generateContent route.

thinking.note: gemini-3.6-flash exposes thinkingLevel minimal/low/medium/high and no off switch. Measured on the direct Google endpoint at thinkingLevel=minimal over an action_time run: 96.5% of calls returned thought tokens, median 1,033 per call, 94% of all output tokens were thoughts. So the model reasons where the open-weight roster is held at thinking=disabled; usageMetadata.thoughtsTokenCount records the actual state per call and must be reported with the scores.

_note: Gemini-native static video, inline base64. The frame rate is not set here:
the adapter sends videoMetadata.fps from each dimension's protocol.frames
spec (2 fps clips, 1 fps action_time episodes), identical to what the local
adapters sample at. Set api.video_fps only to pin or (0) to drop it.
Agentic video (tools.videoRetrieval) is deliberately not enabled: no other
model in the roster may re-query its input.
Key: the adapter default x-goog-api-key header, which is what the relay's
own docs say its Gemini-native entry reads (docs.yunzhuhub.com/clients/
gemini-cli); the same relay also accepted Authorization: Bearer in the
probe (set key_header / key_prefix to switch). Never in the URL.
/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent for Gemini format, no Files API,
no streamGenerateContent, and no stated body-size limit.
max_request_bytes: Google documents 20 MB as the inline threshold; the relay
accepted a 30 MB body in the probe, its ceiling is unmeasured. Raise after
checking the longest action_time episode, media is shrunk spatially to fit.
Acceptance check before any full run: usageMetadata.promptTokenCount on the
video dimensions must be in the thousands (a 27 s clip at 2 fps is on the
order of 1e4 tokens), not the few hundred that a text-only prompt costs.
